svg.text: Sheet 3 rev 2 — Bench control, gate drivers and the hardware fault limit (one driver board + NUCLEO-H743ZI2 #3)

rev 2, 2026-10-08: 74HC221 non-retriggerable one-shots with the arm key on CLR · isolated breaker drivers with their own isolated DC-DC, pull-UP + inverting (unpowered node = breaker OPEN) · all drivers from a separate 12 V adapter · demo-controller output to the HIL · option-C-only parts dashed
enable = thermal switch 90 °C (NC) AND arm key
enable for all five load drivers
→ Q_f8 gate (feeder-side fault, Sheet 1) — option C only
ARM key switch → CLR of U15A and U15B
(CLR low = output forced low; the '221 does not
trigger on the CLR rising edge, unlike the '123)
also: arm-key sense input to the MCU (firmware refuses a fault when the key is off) and the key in series with the
U16 / U17 enable. Three independent cuts: key on CLR, key in the enable, 5 ms by R·C. No firmware state can hold a short.
→ HIL digital input (fault scenario trigger) + SYNC — demo controller (F8)
high side, source at the 12 V node
output (−) tied to the FET's source
high side, source at the 48 V line · option C only
output (−) tied to the FET's source
Truth table (both breakers): node pin floating (unpowered, reset, cable off) → pull-up → IN− high → gate LOW → breaker OPEN (fail-safe).
TRIP = 0 (node running, no fault) → gate HIGH (15 V above the source) → breaker CLOSED. TRIP = 1 → gate LOW → breaker OPEN.
Firmware stays TRIP-active-high as built (board.h PF13). rev 1 wrote 'pull-down + inverting'; that would close the breaker on a dead node.
Why isolated: Q_brk's source sits at 12 V (high side); a ground-referenced 12 V driver gives Vgs ≈ 0 and the FET works as a 35 W source follower,
then fails in linear mode at 100 A. The isolated driver's secondary rides on the source. Same part for Q_fb (option C), whose source rides on 48 V.
Alternative rejected: P-channel high side (≥ 9 mΩ at 40 V class, +10 % in the bolted-fault loop, hot).
ADC3 on v_out (1 MSa/s): < 9.6 V for 100 µs → all LOAD gates low; re-enable above 10.1 V (the model's POL UVLO, V_uvlo48
one pulse at each scheduled event, manual step and fault trigger → feeder node PF12, rack node PF12, scope ch1; from the
12-bit, 1 MSa/s replay tables from tools/replay_waveforms.py → the node's SMA i / SMA v (latency test, Sheet 2 JP1 / JP2
dashboard fault command → one GPIO → HIL digital input (fault scenario trigger in the model) + SYNC; makes the 'trigger
a fault' button work without a PC link to the HIL
tools/bench_run.py scripts the SCALING_SHEET §6 plan: 200 benign events, 60 rack faults (+ 20 feeder faults under option
C); every run recorded by both nodes and the scope
DRIVER SUPPLY ⑤: separate 12 V / 2 A adapter through a 1 A fuse → U10–U14, U16, U17 and the two isolated DC-DCs (U20, U21). NOT the bench bus:
a bolted fault pulls the 12 V bus to ≈ 5 V in 5 ms (linear-mode gates), and opening Q_brk removes it. Logic 3.3 V from the Nucleo. Common ground with the bench star.
Adapter off ⇒ both breakers open (fail-safe holds through the supply path too).
Scope: ch1 SYNC · ch2 rack shunt (differential probe ≥ 10 MHz across R_sh2, before the node's filter) · ch3 ONSET (PF14) · ch4 TRIP (PF13) → onset-to-trip latency and the raw fault front.

Scope ground clips on the star only. HIL mode: SYNC comes from a HIL digital output into PF12 (level-shift if the HIL output is 5 V / 24 V); both TRIPs go to HIL digital inputs (buffer per the input threshold).

Parts on this sheet (rev 2): 7 × TC4420 / UCC27517 · 2 × UCC5350 (or ADuM4120) · 2 × isolated DC-DC 12 → 15 V 1 W · 1 × 74HC221 · key switch · 12 V 2 A adapter + 1 A fuse · thermal switch 90 °C NC · R/C for the one-shots (1 % / C0G or film).
Option B drops U16, U18, U20, U15A and their R/C. The MCU can only START a fault pulse; its length is set by R_t·C_t in the one-shot, the arm key sits on CLR and in the enable.
